title: Kornati Itinerary 2027: 1, 2 and 3-Day Plans, Costs
metaDescription: Kornati itinerary for 2027: day trips from Zadar and Murter, 2–3 day sailing routes, park ticket rules, konobas, swim stops and real costs in euros.
content:
## What Is the Best Itinerary for Kornati?

Kornati National Park covers 89 islands, islets and reefs, which makes it the densest archipelago in the Mediterranean. There is no bridge and no scheduled ferry. Every visit is by boat, so the itinerary depends on how much time you have and whether you travel on a tour or on your own vessel.

- **1 day:** a group boat tour from Murter, Zadar, Biograd, Vodice, Šibenik or Pakoštane.
- **2 days:** a skippered or self-drive boat from Murter with one night in a bay on Kornat.
- **3 days:** a sailing loop through the central and southern islands with a stop in Telašćica.

## Where to Start: Murter, Zadar or Šibenik

Murter is the closest gateway. Tour boats leave the main harbour (Hramina bay) at about 09:00 and return around 17:30–18:00. The park boundary is close, so more of the day is spent in the islands.

Zadar has the most tour choice. Boats take about 40 minutes by fast boat to reach the area, and many itineraries pair Kornati with Telašćica Nature Park on Dugi Otok. Zadar day trips are priced from about €30 on large boats to €65–70 on smaller operators. Speedboat tours cost more, at around €110–155.

Biograd na Moru, Pakoštane, Vodice and Šibenik also have departures. Šibenik tours run higher, and small-group trips there cost well over €100.

From Zadar to Murter, the bus takes about 56 minutes and costs roughly €4–8. Murter suits anyone who wants to stay close to the departure point and rent a boat.

## One-Day Kornati Itinerary (Group Tour)

A typical full-day tour follows this pattern:

1. **09:00 departure** from the harbour.
2. **Morning cruise** past the outer cliffs on the seaward side of Kornat, known as the "crowns". These cliffs drop straight into the sea and are the main sight for photographers.
3. **First swim stop.** On Murter tours this is often Rašip or Modri bok bay on Kornat, with about 90 minutes at the first stop.
4. **Lunch** in a bay such as Vrulje, a small fishing settlement with time to walk around. Lunch is usually fish, meat or a vegetarian option with a drink.
5. **Second stop** on Levrnaka, which has a short walk to a viewpoint.
6. **Return** to the harbour around 17:30–18:00.

From Zadar, tours often include Telašćica, with the cliffs along the Dugi Otok coast and a swim in Mir salt lake. Other stops are Lojena beach on Kornat and Sakarun beach on Dugi Otok for speedboat trips.

Tour prices usually include the park ticket, lunch, a guide and a welcome drink. The park fee itself costs group operators about €7 per person in season, so it is a small part of the price.

### What to Pick on a Group Tour

Book a smaller or older wooden boat if you can. Large boats carry up to 150 passengers, with more noise and crowding at the lunch stop. Small boats cost more but spend more time swimming.

## Two-Day Kornati Itinerary (Murter Base)

A two-day plan works with a private skippered boat or a rented licence-free boat from Murter. A skippered boat for 1–6 people costs about €450 per day, and for 7–14 people about €600. These prices include fuel, skipper and the park ticket. Self-drive boats without a licence (up to 6 people) cost from about €130 per day on top of the park ticket and fuel.

**Day 1:** Leave Murter in the morning. Swim at Opat and the northern islands, then head south along the inside of Kornat. Stop at Levrnaka for the viewpoint walk. Overnight in a sheltered bay on Kornat with a konoba and mooring buoys, such as Vrulje, Statival or Lojena.

**Day 2:** Take the morning swim before the day boats arrive, around 08:00–10:00. Cruise through the outer islands, then exit via the Proversa pass or return through the inner channel to Murter by late afternoon.

## Three-Day Kornati Sailing Itinerary

A three-day sail suits yachts and charter groups.

- **Day 1:** Murter to the northern Kornati, swim at Opat, then moor in Vrulje or a similar northern bay.
- **Day 2:** Move south through the central islands. Visit Levrnaka and the Kornat interior bays, then continue towards Telašćica on Dugi Otok.
- **Day 3:** Walk to the Telašćica cliffs and Mir salt lake. Return to Murter or continue to Zadar.

The park ticket is valid per day. A 3-day or 7-day ticket costs less than three single days and also covers other parks. Kornati's own ticket pages list longer-validity options. Check the current class for your boat length.

## Park Ticket Prices for Your Own Boat

Admission is charged per boat, per day, not per person. The cheapest class is a small boat under 7 m, which costs €25 in low season and €45 in high season when bought in advance. Larger boats are priced by length. A boat of 11–17.99 m costs €150 in the cheaper period and €300 in the higher one. A boat of 18–24.99 m costs €240 or €480.

Buy tickets online before you enter. Mobile ranger desks inside the park charge roughly double. Free mooring buoys come with a valid ticket.

## Best Time to Visit

The best swimming season is June to September, with sea temperatures of 20–27°C. July and August are busiest, so book tours 2–3 days ahead. May, June and September give calmer anchorages and cheaper low-season tickets.

## Local Tips and Opinion

Most visitors overestimate how much they will see on a single day tour. Day boats cover only a small part of the archipelago, mostly the same few bays. If you have the budget, a skippered boat for two days gives much better value than a second tour.

- **Check wind forecasts.** The bora wind from the northeast can cancel tours and make anchorages unsafe. Tour operators decide on the day.
- **Bring cash.** Onboard bars on larger boats often accept cash only.
- **Bring water and sun protection.** There are almost no shops, no shade on many islands and no drinking water on the walks.
- **Bring shoes with grip.** The karst limestone is sharp and hot by midday.
- **Eat in a konoba.** The few seasonal konobas in the bays serve fish, lamb and local olive oil. Many are open only in season and some accept moored boats only.
- **Go early.** Choose departures at 09:00 or earlier to reach swim stops before the crowds.

## Sample Budget (Per Person)

| Plan | Cost |
|---|---|
| Budget day tour from Zadar | €30–50 |
| Mid-range tour from Murter or Biograd | €60–65 |
| Private skippered boat, 4 people | About €112 each |
| Skippered boat, 2 days, 4 people, plus mooring and meals | About €250–300 each |

## How to Get There Without a Boat

No public ferry reaches the park. Bus services connect Zadar and Murter four times a day. Use the bus to reach the harbour and join a day tour. Murter and Zadar have rooms and apartments near the departure points, so a night before the tour makes the 09:00 departure easy.

faq.question: How many days do you need in Kornati?
faq.answer: One day is enough to see the main sights on a boat tour. Two or three days on a private or sailing boat give much more time in quieter bays and are better value for small groups.

faq.question: How much does a Kornati day trip cost?
faq.answer: Group tours cost about €30–70 per person depending on the departure point and the boat. Murter tours are often €60–65. Prices usually include the park ticket, lunch and a welcome drink.

faq.question: Can you visit Kornati without a boat?
faq.answer: Not independently. There is no bridge and no scheduled ferry. Organised tours depart from Murter, Zadar, Šibenik, Vodice, Biograd and Pakoštane.

faq.question: How is the Kornati park ticket charged?
faq.answer: The ticket is charged per boat per day, not per person. A boat under 7 m costs €25 in low season and €45 in high season if bought online in advance. Buying inside the park costs about double.

faq.question: What is the best time to visit Kornati?
faq.answer: June to September is the best period for swimming, with sea temperatures of 20–27°C. May, June and September are less crowded than July and August.

faq.question: Is it better to visit Kornati from Zadar or Murter?
faq.answer: Murter is closer, so tours spend more time among the islands. Zadar has more operators and often adds Telašćica Nature Park, but the day is longer on the water.

faq.question: Where can you eat in Kornati?
faq.answer: Most day tours include lunch in a bay such as Vrulje. Seasonal konobas in bays on Kornat serve fish and meat, but they are open mainly in summer and book out in July and August.

quickAnswer: A one-day Kornati itinerary starts at Murter, Zadar, Biograd or Šibenik. It takes a 9-hour boat tour with 2–3 swim stops, lunch and the park ticket included, usually for €35–65 per person. For more time, sail or rent a boat for 2–3 days and overnight in Kornat's bays.
